target_customer: Restaurants and small food businesses buying wholesale food and supplies; during 2020 also consumers
problem: Restaurant owners found sourcing and ordering from incumbent distributors manual, opaque on prices and poorly serviced. Cheetah offers a catalog with next day delivery from its own warehouse and fleet.
business_model: vertically integrated wholesale food distribution (margin on goods sold)

founders.name: Na'ama Moran
previous_startups: a local commerce startup acquired by Groupon (unnamed)
founders.background_notes: Grew up in Israel in a family of farmers and small business owners, per the 2022 Restaurant Technology News interview.

founders.name: Alon Har-Tal
founders.background_notes: Per the 2022 interview; named as founder in TechCrunch 2020.

founders.name: Christopher Elliott
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in TechCrunch 2020-04-28; not on the YC page.

founders.name: Vincent Matranga
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in TechCrunch 2020-04-28; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Later required catalog, purchasing, warehouse and routing systems; the YC era product was an ordering and delivery app.

defensibility.rationale: Physical distribution has capital intensity but broadline distributors and delivery apps compete on the same restaurants.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying Cheetah; in 2020 restaurant demand collapsed in COVID and Cheetah pivoted to consumers.

market_need_then: Interview says restaurant owners found sourcing manual and distributors poor on pricing transparency and service while shopping easily on Amazon personally.

branding.name_origin: Reflects the goal of becoming the fastest growing foodservice distributor, and that cheetahs hunt in packs, inspiring the Cheetah Coalition of small restaurants (2022 interview).

identity.visual_style: colorful fleet of delivery vehicles (per one search summary)
identity.voice_and_tone: Playful, with a Cheetah+ loyalty program and chef perks.

branding.brand_signature: Cheetah Coalition and Cheetah+ loyalty program
branding.community_and_virality: Chef appreciation nights and a loyalty program on the company site; no independent fan evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: A fast, memorable animal name tied to a coalition idea and loyalty perks, but the name is shared with many unrelated companies and there is little independent brand press.

pivots.to: Cheetah For Me, consumer grocery pickup and delivery
pivots.why: Restaurant wholesale business with about 3,000 customers largely stopped as restaurants closed in COVID-19 (TechCrunch 2020-04-28).

outcome_analysis: Cheetah entered YC in Winter 2013 and later built a vertically integrated food distributor serving thousands of restaurants, raising a 36 million dollar Series B in 2020 and a 60 million dollar Series C in 2022. COVID closures forced a consumer pivot, and a search headline suggests the physical distribution business is being sold to Palo Alto Foods, which is unconfirmed here. No exit is confirmed.
notes: Date conflict: the 2022 interview says Cheetah was founded in 2015 in Pleasanton while the YC page lists Winter 2013; the YC page's Crunchbase slug 'sourcery' may indicate an earlier name, unconfirmed. The YC era product was a small business delivery service, details not found. Series A of about 30M in 2018-10 and a 14M round in 2024 appear only on aggregators (startupintros, search summaries), so unverified and not recorded; total raised stated as 66M by TechCrunch after Series B. A headline of an unconfirmed sale of the distribution business to Palo Alto Foods was seen only in a URL. Competitors left empty: no source dated near 2013 found; 2020 article names Choco and Instacart, noted here only. The Series C stage and amount come from the interview and FSR Magazine headline; investors from the interview.
